Fixes #30234
Part of #3146 · Ruling-ref: 6629858351 (maintainer, 2026-11-04, 「同意，企业版功能在 cloud 中立卡后续开发」)

Clause-②: no (docs only, an ADR; the protocol addition rides #30235)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — docs only and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the two passages of `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` that teach "the trash surface is retired" and "there is no recycle bin" stay true until the engine slice ships, so their rewrite is owed by #30235 / #30237, not by this record
Prior rulings read: recycle bin,softdelete,trash,retention → 3 hits; ADR-0006 D1, ADR-0045 Decision §6, ADR-0131 D1; thread: none; repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：新增 `docs/adr/0148-recycle-bin-separate-store-restore-under-original-ids-retention-in-days.md`，把你 2026-11-04 在 #3146 上的裁决（回收站独立存储、每次删除一条记录、按原 id 恢复、保留期按天经宿主钩子、企业层放 cloud）记成正式 ADR；ADR-0049 的 `**Status**:` 行末尾追加一条日期注记，说明旧键保持移除；`docs/adr/README.md` 由 `scripts/adr-index.mjs` 重新生成。无代码、无 schema、无生成产物。
- **为什么改**：#3146 拆出的三张子卡（#30235 spec、#30237 engine、#30239 UI）都要引用一份 ADR；ADR-0049 当年因无读者删掉了 `enable.trash` / `softDelete` / `allowRestore` / `allowPurge`，新面必须先把未来的读者逐项点名，否则又是「声明而不执行」。
- **风险与回滚**：仅文档，回滚即 revert 本 PR。记录里每项机制都写成「已裁决、待落地」并点名承载卡，不声称任何已上线行为；ADR-0049 的决策正文一字未动。
- **先看**：① ADR-0148 的 D1（为什么选独立存储而不是 `IsDeleted` 列）、D3（天数与宿主钩子，框架只知天数不知套餐）、D5（新面 → 读者 → 承载卡的表，以及旧键保持墓碑：按 ADR-0087 的 kit 规则，`allowRestore` / `allowPurge` 的 kit 在 18 仍保留、19 退出，`enable.trash` kit 的转换已在 18 切版时移除，两者都不在加载路径上重放）、D7（记录自己定下、裁决未定的几项选择，逐项标明）；② ADR-0049 第 3 行状态行末尾的注记；③ 「Where "days, never plans" is written down」一节——仓内没有 ADR 写下这条原则，它写在 `resolveFeatures` 接缝的注释里并引用 cloud ADR-0012。
- **两分钟验证**：在本分支跑 `pnpm check:adr-index && pnpm check:adr-links && pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors`，预期三条全绿，索引显示 149 条记录、ADR-0148 状态为 Accepted。
- **需要你做的**：`docs/adr/**` 是 Tier H，需要你 Approve（或亲手合并）；席位不会排队、不会开 auto-merge。

## What changes

- **New `docs/adr/0148-recycle-bin-separate-store-restore-under-original-ids-retention-in-days.md`** (427 lines). It records the ruling in the ruling's own terms; where it fixes a name the ruling offered as an example or settles something the ruling left open, it says so at that point and lists each such choice once in D7. Status `Accepted — 2026-11-05`, with the sentence "This record declares; it implements nothing": nothing in it ships on `main`, and every mechanism is worded as decided and planned, with its tracking card.
- **`docs/adr/0049-no-unenforced-security-properties.md`**: one dated amendment note appended to the end of its `**Status**:` line (the line still starts `**Status**:`; the keyword `Accepted` is unmoved). The note points at ADR-0148 and says the removed keys stay removed — tombstones stand; under ADR-0087's kit rule the `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` kit (`entries/18`, retired after 17.2.0) is carried at 18 and ages out at 19, the `enable.trash` kit's conversion was removed when 18 was cut and only its tombstone remains, neither replays at load (both `retiredFromLoadPath`); `softDelete` never had one. The decision text is untouched.
- **`docs/adr/README.md`**: regenerated by `node scripts/adr-index.mjs` (the index is generated, not hand-kept): 148 → 149 records, 143 → 144 numbers, one new row.

### Where each ruling item is recorded

| Ruling 6629858351 | ADR-0148 |
|---|---|
| 1. A separate recycle-bin store, not a `deleted_at` column; one entry per delete operation; the cascade set snapshotted; the delete stays physical; every read path untouched; why not Salesforce's `IsDeleted` | D1 — Shape |
| Restore under the original ids; `created_by` / `created_at` kept; its own restored event, never a create; the three refusals (unique taken, parent purged, package uninstalled); lookup re-link only when unchanged since; flow enrollments not restored; rollups recompute; a cascaded child not restored alone; a person restores what they deleted, an admin sees all | D2 — Restore |
| 2. Open source owns the mechanism; retention in days, default 30, `OS_RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS`; a host resolver hook on the `resolveFeatures` pattern; days, never plans; TTL purge on the LifecycleService following the `sys_file` tombstone; permanent delete never enters the bin | D3 — Retention |
| 3. Cloud sets per-plan retention (Free 7 / Team+ 30) through the hook; the enterprise layer (per-object retention, legal hold, longer retention, audit reports, bulk restore, erasure proof) is a cloud card | D3 and Provenance |
| Proposed v1 scope (in / refusals / lookups / forward-only / later); risks (restore fidelity, delete latency, bin storage shown separately, privacy: FLS on listing, secret fields out or encrypted, purge on organization or environment deletion) | D4 — v1 scope, forward-only, later items, and the privacy rules |
| "It needs an ADR, or an ADR-0049 amendment, naming the readers that will exist … new keys, not the tombstoned ones" | D5 — the readers table (surface → reader → card: #30235 / #30237 / #30239 / the cloud card) and "The old keys stay retired"; plus the ADR-0049 status note |
| What the record fixes that the ruling offered as an example or left open: the names `sys_recycle_bin` and `OS_RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS`; the hook's input, output and validation; the purge deadline stamped on the entry at delete time; the entry stored by the default datasource; secret fields out of the snapshot in v1; the `restored` event's name and the grant keys added to #30235's scope; no object-level authoring key (by rule, not by a flag); the privacy rules as standing rules that bind v1 and everything after it | D7 — each marked as the record's choice where it is made |
| What the record leaves to the cards (the remaining spellings, the bulk cap, the Console's wording, the cloud card's shape) | D6 |

### Measurements this record is built on

- **Next free ADR number.** `main` (bb86ff96) ends at ADR-0147. Every one of the 34 open PRs was read for a `docs/adr/01NN-*.md` it adds — #29866 (the one open `docs(adr)` PR) amends ADR-0015 and adds no record; the 17 other non-mailbox PRs, the 15 mailbox PRs and the Version Packages PR add none (each head's `docs/adr/` tree listed). 0148 is free.
- **ADR-0049's removals**, read from the tombstones rather than the card: `enable.trash` and `softDelete` removed in the 16.x line (#2377; `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, which still says "there is no soft-delete/recycle-bin runtime … Deletes are hard deletes"); `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` removed with #12497 (the permission-schema tombstone says `@objectstack/spec` 17, the conversion entry `permission-allow-restore-purge-removed.ts` says protocol 18; the ADR cites the card number and not a version). The card's "removed in 16.0" is therefore exact for two of the four keys; the record reads the code.
- **"The framework knows days, never plans (ADR-0012)."** No ADR under `docs/adr/` states it (grep for `resolveFeatures`, "plan-agnostic", "plan name": zero hits). This repository's ADR-0012 is the messaging platform. The principle is written in the docblock of `packages/cloud-connection/src/runtime-config-plugin.ts` ("Feature seam (open-core boundary — cloud ADR-0012)": the open package owns the mechanism; which billing plan unlocks a key is a distribution concern never enumerated in the framework; hosts inject through `resolveFeatures`, which takes an opaque token — cloud passes the plan string — and returns an open-ended map merged verbatim) and in the package's 9.5.0 changelog entry ("plan-agnostic"). The nearest ADR here is ADR-0132 D2. So the ruling's "ADR-0012" is cloud ADR-0012; the record says so in its Provenance and in a section of its own, and cites it as Prime Directive #13 spells a cloud record.
- **Code the ruling names**, cited by path: `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-cascade.ts` (`collectCascadeDeleteSet`, `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade`), `packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts` and `packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts` (the `sys_file` tombstone and its 30-day reap), `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts` (`LifecycleService`), `packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts` (`releaseSecretHandles`, #27581), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts` (`DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS`, `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION`). No line anchors.

## Why

The maintainer unparked #3146 on 2026-11-04 with the recycle-bin shape, and triage split it into four children chained by `Blocked-by:`; this card is the first, and the p1 spec card #30235 cannot start without a record to cite. ADR-0049 removed the earlier soft-delete keys because nothing read them; a new surface under the same policy has to name its readers before it is declared, which is what D5 does.

## Acceptance notes

- **Observation, not carded:** #3146's body cites `docs/audits/2026-06-objectschema-property-liveness.md`, which is not on `main` (the June 2026 sheets present are `appschema`, `security-identity`, `validationschema` and `record-search`). ADR-0148 cites the audit by its card (#1878) and the `docs/audits/` directory instead of the missing path. A dead citation in an issue body is not one of the three carded classes.
- **Observation, not carded:** the card and the ruling say all four keys were "removed in 16.0 under ADR-0049"; the spec's own tombstones date `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` to #12497 (spec 17 / protocol 18). The record reads the tombstones. No metadata author is misled: both spellings are refused with the same prescription.
- **Owed elsewhere (Skills-docs line):** `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` teaches "the trash surface is retired" and "there is no recycle bin". Both stay true until #30237 ships; the rewrite rides #30235 / #30237 under their own `Skills-docs:` lines.
- **Deviation, reported:** the session's harness asks for a model-named `Co-Authored-By` trailer; the commit carries the repository's model-free pair (`Co-authored-by: Claude` + `Claude-Session:`), which the pre-push hook requires.
- **Deviation, reported:** the harness's post-create step (assign the requester, request their review) is skipped on purpose: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` rule 2 keeps the PR's people with the seat at hand-over, and `pr_create` went out with no assignees and no reviewers.
